/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 14 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3195 (6)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5316 (-24)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2503 (49)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1558 (5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 851 (3)
CAPESIZE
Ascension Day resulted in a quieter overall session, with the market pausing slightly following the strong gains seen earlier in the week. The BCI 182 5TC eased by $224 to close at $48,209, as sentiment across both basins became a touch more measured despite generally healthy underlying cargo volumes. In the Pacific, activity levels remained solid overall, although the tone turned slightly mixed as miner resistance became more apparent throughout the day. Two miners were initially active on C5, although one was later reported to have temporised, contributing to softer sentiment into the close. Offers on C5 began the session around the $16.00 mark before gradually slipping into the high $15s, with one miner reportedly bidding closer to $14.50. By the close, offers had moved into the low $15s, although no fixtures had been reported at the time of writing. Consequently, C5 slipped by 0.457 to $15.433. The Atlantic basin presented a similarly mixed picture. The North Atlantic remained comparatively firm, supported by stronger transatlantic activity, with a notable fixture helping push C8 up by $2,625 to $56,938. However, South Brazil and West Africa to China business softened marginally, with limited fresh activity reported on C3. Bid levels were heard around $36 against low $37s for index dates, leaving C3 marginally higher by $0.202 at $36.925.
PANAMAX
Another day of positive momentum in the Panamax market across the Atlantic basin, although overall activity was slightly subdued due to the widespread European holiday. The trans Atlantic market maintained its upward trajectory, with brokers highlighting its close correlation to the strength in the fronthaul market, alongside an increase in both mineral and grain volumes. The fronthaul sector continued to show a firm trend, with multiple fixtures reported, albeit at a slower pace compared to previous sessions. In the Pacific, sentiment appeared more mixed. Some market participants noted a remaining demand for prompt tonnage in Southeast Asia, particularly for mineral runs from Indonesia and Australia. However, others suggested the market may be pausing as charterers reassess fundamentals and pull back on bids. The Bettys Love (77,171 2008) open in Tianjin 15/17 May was reported as fixed for a trip with coal via East Coast Australia to South China with the rate discussed as between $20,500 and $22,250 to Guaransea. The Zhong Chang Zhou Shan (75,409 2013) open in Gunsan 27/30 May was reported to have been placed on subjects for period of a minimum duration of 25 October to a maximum of 25 December 2026 at $19,300, although the charterer remained unknown. The P5TC increased by $445 concluding to $22,528.
SUPRAMAX
With the widespread European holiday unsurprisingly, it was a rather slow day in the Atlantic and brokers said that fundamentals changed little in the Atlantic. Asia remained buoyant, with the north maintaining demand and some reasonable levels being discussed. The Yun Tong Hai (64,708 2025) open Caofeidian 20 May was heard fixed for a trip to West Africa at $24,500 but no more details came to light. The Sea Aquarius (53,468 2006) open Zhoushan 23/25 May was heard fixed also to West Africa in low $19,000s, again no more details were disclosed. The Astro Vega (63,008 2015) Huludao 15/18 May was heard fixed $21,500 for a trip Thailand with steel, again further details remained lacking. Period activity surfaced, the Britian Bay (58,709 2012) Mizushima 17/19 May was said to have been placed on subjects at $19,000 for 4/6 months trading. The 11TC average closed up $73 at $19,698.

HANDYSIZE
The market delivered another mixed session, with weakness in Atlantic side due to holidays offset by modest gains in Pacific. The BHSI rose 3 points to 851, while the 7TC average increased by $56 to close at $15,311. In both the Continent and Mediterranean, only minor changes were recorded, with rates easing slightly from previous levels. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic and US Gulf were notably quiet, with limited reported activity and rates beginning to soften. In contrast, Asia maintained a healthy pace of trading, with owners and charterers gradually lifting their rate ideas. A 38,000-dwt vessel open in the Philippines was fixed via West Australia to the Far East at $17,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Brazil Soybean Exports Eye New May Record

Brazil’s soybean export pace continues to strengthen, with ANEC raising its May forecast to 16.0 Mt from 14.5 Mt last week, putting shipments on track for a record May volume. The revised estimate would mark a 12.7% year-on-year increase, while cumulative soybean exports for January-May are projected at 59.1 Mt, up 8.9% from 2025 levels. Soybean meal exports are also expected to surge 35.6% year-on-year to 2.9 Mt, reflecting firm global demand. Meanwhile, May corn exports are forecast at 308,570 tonnes, well above last year’s 68,400 tonnes.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve lost value today in response to a negative index, with the Pacific drifting lower while the Atlantic market remains tight. The Jun contract was the heaviest with 37650 sold, followed by the May contract with 41750 sold. The May v Jun contract continues to widen and strengthen trading north of 4000. Jul was under pressure also with 34250 trading, while the Q3 struggled for liquidity trading within a range of 33000-33300. Q4 was relatively inactive today with a small clip done at 31850. Cal27 closed marginally weaker also, with 26650 sold.

PMX
The PMX market was quieter today, with the curve finding some support through the morning before easing back off into the close. May traded in a narrow range of 21650–21700, holding steady throughout the session. June remained the main point of interest, trading 22250–22650 and seeing the most activity, but values softened back towards the close to 22100. July bounced around 21550 and 22000. Q3 traded 20650–21000. Further out, Q4 printed 18650–18850, while Nov saw a single print at 18900. Cal 27 remained steady in a tight range of 15425–15550.

SMX + HANDY
SMX had a slower session today, with most of the activity focused around the front months. June was the standout contract, trading between 19000 and 19300, while May held at 17900. July traded in a narrower 19000–19200 range
